quests.sentence: She had finished the report.
quests.ruleExplanation: Had finished pairs the past-perfect helper had with the past participle to show a completed-before-then action, followed by the object the report.
quests.nativeTip: Had plus the past participle marks an action completed before another past point, followed by the object.

quests.sentence: They had completed the training.
quests.ruleExplanation: Had completed follows They the same way it would follow any subject, since had doesn't change form for singular or plural.
quests.nativeTip: Had works the same way for every subject — no had/has split like present perfect has.

quests.sentence: He had signed the contract.
quests.ruleExplanation: Had signed follows He, with the contract as the object, confirming had never changes form.
quests.nativeTip: The same had-plus-past-participle pattern applies regardless of subject.

quests.sentence: She hadn't finished the paperwork.
quests.ruleExplanation: Hadn't replaces had not right before finished, with the report completing the object.
quests.nativeTip: Hadn't fuses had and not, sitting directly before the past participle.

quests.sentence: They hadn't received the invoice.
quests.ruleExplanation: Hadn't precedes received, with the invoice as the object, following the negative past-perfect pattern.
quests.nativeTip: The same contraction works for any subject, right before the past participle.

quests.sentence: He hadn't seen the email.
quests.ruleExplanation: Hadn't precedes seen, with the email as the object.
quests.nativeTip: Hadn't still comes right before the past participle, regardless of subject.

quests.sentence: Had she finished the report?
quests.ruleExplanation: Had moves ahead of she to form the question, with finished the report following in normal order.
quests.nativeTip: Move had to the front of the sentence, ahead of the subject, to ask the question.

quests.sentence: Had they received the payment?
quests.ruleExplanation: Had leads the question before they, followed by received the payment.
quests.nativeTip: Had inverts with the subject the same way for any subject type.

quests.sentence: Had he already left the building?
quests.ruleExplanation: Had opens the question before he, and already sits right before left, with the building as the object.
quests.nativeTip: Already can appear inside a past-perfect question too, sitting between the subject and the past participle.

quests.sentence: She had already left the office.
quests.ruleExplanation: Already fits between had and left, in the same mid-position it occupies in present perfect sentences.
quests.nativeTip: Already sits between had and the past participle, just as it does with present perfect.

quests.sentence: They had already signed the agreement.
quests.ruleExplanation: Already sits between had and signed, with the agreement as the object.
quests.nativeTip: The same mid-position holds regardless of subject or verb.

quests.sentence: He had already reviewed the documents.
quests.ruleExplanation: Already fits between had and reviewed, with the documents as the object.
quests.nativeTip: Already keeps its fixed spot right before the past participle.

quests.sentence: She had finished the report before her meeting started.
quests.ruleExplanation: She had finished the report describes the earlier completed action, and before her meeting started names the later event that it happened ahead of.
quests.nativeTip: The past perfect clause (the earlier event) comes first, then before introduces the later, simple-past event.

quests.sentence: They had left the building before a fire alarm rang.
quests.ruleExplanation: They had left the building is the earlier action, and before a fire alarm rang is the later event, introduced by before.
quests.nativeTip: The earlier event (past perfect) still leads, followed by before and the later, simple-past event.

quests.sentence: He had eaten dinner before his guests arrived.
quests.ruleExplanation: He had eaten dinner is the earlier action, and before his guests arrived names the later event using simple past.
quests.nativeTip: The same order holds: past perfect for what happened first, then before plus the later simple-past event.

quests.sentence: After she had finished the paperwork, she left for home.
quests.ruleExplanation: After she had finished the report fronts the earlier action, followed by a comma and she left for home, the later simple-past event.
quests.nativeTip: After can front the earlier event in past perfect — after-clause, comma, then the later simple-past main clause.

quests.sentence: After they had signed the agreement, they shook hands.
quests.ruleExplanation: After they had signed the agreement fronts the earlier event, followed by a comma and they shook hands, the resulting simple-past action.
quests.nativeTip: The same fronting pattern applies: after-clause with had, comma, then the simple-past result.

quests.sentence: After he had checked the numbers, he approved our budget.
quests.ruleExplanation: After he had checked the numbers fronts the earlier action, followed by a comma and he approved our budget, the resulting event.
quests.nativeTip: The fronted after-clause still uses had, followed by a comma and the simple-past main clause.

quests.sentence: She had already left by the time he arrived.
quests.ruleExplanation: She had already left is the completed action, and by the time he arrived names the later simple-past moment it was already true by.
quests.nativeTip: By the time introduces the later simple-past event, and the past perfect clause before it states what had already happened.

quests.sentence: They had finished dinner by the time we arrived.
quests.ruleExplanation: They had finished dinner is the completed action, and by the time we arrived marks the later reference point.
quests.nativeTip: The same pattern holds: past perfect first, then by the time plus the later simple-past event.

quests.sentence: He had solved his problem by the time support called.
quests.ruleExplanation: He had solved his problem is the completed action, and by the time support called marks the later moment.
quests.nativeTip: By the time still marks the later reference point, after the past perfect states what was already true.

quests.sentence: Before their meeting started, she had already finished the report.
quests.ruleExplanation: Before their meeting started fronts the later simple-past event, followed by a comma and she had already finished the report, the earlier completed action.
quests.nativeTip: Before can also front the later, simple-past event — before-clause, comma, then the earlier past-perfect main clause.

quests.sentence: Before a fire alarm rang, they had already left the building.
quests.ruleExplanation: Before a fire alarm rang fronts the later event, followed by a comma and they had already left the building, the earlier completed action.

quests.sentence: Before his guests arrived, he had already prepared dinner.

quests.sentence: When he arrived, she had already left.
quests.ruleExplanation: When he arrived fronts the later event, followed by a comma and she had already left, the earlier completed action — the reverse pairing from File 8's when-plus-past-continuous.
quests.nativeTip: When fronts the later simple-past event, and the earlier action uses past perfect with already after the comma.

quests.sentence: When the manager checked, her team had already fixed that issue.
quests.ruleExplanation: When the manager checked fronts the later event, and her team had already fixed the issue names the earlier completed action.
quests.nativeTip: The same when-plus-past-perfect pairing shows which of two past events happened first.

quests.sentence: When the plane landed, passengers had already collected their luggage.
quests.ruleExplanation: When the plane landed fronts the later event, and passengers had already collected their luggage names what had already happened by then.
quests.nativeTip: When still marks the later event, with had already marking the action that finished first.

quests.sentence: By the time this movie ended, most viewers had already guessed its twist.
quests.ruleExplanation: By the time the movie ended fronts the later event, and most viewers had already guessed its twist names the earlier completed action, combining two skills from this file.

quests.sentence: After the negotiations had failed, both companies filed lawsuits.

quests.sentence: Before support arrived, the customer had already resolved their issue.
quests.ruleExplanation: Before support arrived fronts the later event, followed by a comma and the customer had already resolved the issue, the earlier completed action.
